items.title: Orange means work zone
items.simple: Orange signs mean a work zone is ahead. Workers may be on the road. Slow down and stay alert.
items.official: Remember, the color orange marks a work zone and means slow down and be alert.
items.mnemonic: Orange = work zone. Slow down, stay alert.

items.title: Work zone speeding: up to $500
items.simple: Workers' lives depend on you. Obey the speed limit in a highway work zone. Speeding there can get you a fine of up to $500.
items.official: If you are convicted of exceeding the speed limit in a highway work zone, you may be fined up to $500.
items.mnemonic: Speeding: up to $500. Phone in hand: half that, $250.

items.title: Handheld phone in work zone: $250
items.simple: Keep the phone out of your hand in a highway work zone. Using a handheld phone there means a $250 fine. Workers need your full attention.
items.official: If you are convicted of using a handheld communications device in a highway work zone, you will be fined $250.
items.mnemonic: Phone in hand: $250. Half the $500 speeding max.

items.title: Rough road or uneven lanes
items.simple: Rough Road, Bump or Uneven Lanes signs mean the road ahead is bumpy. Loose gravel or road work can cause this. Driving there is extra hard for motorcycle riders. Slow down.
items.official: These signs are used when certain road conditions, such as loose gravel or road construction, affect the roadway surface and create potentially difficult conditions for motorists, especially motorcyclists.
items.mnemonic: Bumpy road? Hardest on two wheels.

items.title: Construction ahead and detour
items.simple: Road Construction Ahead and Detour signs mean a change is coming. Your route or the way traffic moves will change. Slow down. Strange or risky conditions are ahead.
items.official: These signs indicate a change in the traffic pattern or route ahead. Slow down. Unusual or potentially dangerous conditions are ahead.

items.title: Flashing arrow boards
items.simple: You see a big flashing arrow board in a work zone. It means part of the road ahead is closed. Move into the lane the arrow points to.
items.official: Large flashing arrow boards or flashing message signs in work zones direct drivers to proceed into different traffic lanes and inform them that part of the road ahead is closed.

items.title: Flaggers: who they are
items.simple: Flaggers are road workers who direct traffic. They usually wear orange or yellow vests, or yellow-green shirts or jackets. A sign with a worker holding a flag means a flagger is ahead.
items.official: Flaggers are highway workers who normally wear orange or yellow vests, or yellow-green shirts or jackets.
items.mnemonic: Flaggers dress bright: orange, yellow or yellow-green.

items.title: Obey flagger STOP/SLOW paddles
items.simple: Flaggers hold STOP and SLOW paddles or red flags. If the flagger shows STOP, you stop. SLOW means go slowly and carefully. Flaggers also stop traffic so workers and work trucks can cross.
items.official: They use STOP/SLOW paddles or red flags to stop or direct traffic through the work zone, and to let other workers or construction vehicles cross the road.
items.mnemonic: The paddle is the boss. STOP side, you stop.

items.title: Work zone photo speed enforcement
items.simple: This sign means cameras catch speeders in the work zone. Always obey the posted work zone speed limit.
items.official: This sign indicates that automated photo enforcement is in place for speeding in a work zone. Always obey the posted speed limit in a work zone.

items.title: Near cones: stay centered
items.simple: Cones, drums, barricades and concrete barriers guide you through a work zone. Near them, keep your car in the middle of your lane. Obey the posted speed limit.
items.official: Barricades, vertical signs, concrete barriers, drums and cones are the most common devices used to guide drivers safely through work zones. When driving near the devices, keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit.
items.mnemonic: Cones on the sides, car in the middle.

items.title: Leaving the work zone
items.simple: As you leave a work zone, stay in your lane and keep your speed. Wait to change lanes until you are all the way out.
items.official: As you leave the work zone, stay in your lane and maintain your speed. Don't change lanes until you are completely clear of the work zone.
items.mnemonic: Same lane, same speed, until you are clear.

items.title: Always obey message boards
items.simple: Message boards by the road warn you about traffic, road or weather conditions and other dangers. Always do what they say. Before a trip, call 511 to check for road work.
items.official: They provide information about traffic, road, weather or other hazardous conditions. Always obey any directions posted on these message boards. For information about road conditions or road construction in advance of your trip, visit www.virginiadot.org, www.511virginia.org or call 511.
items.mnemonic: Road work info before a trip? Dial 5-1-1.

items.title: Rumble strips: drive over slowly
items.simple: Rumble strips are black or orange strips across your lane before a work zone. They warn you of a flagger or a closed lane. Drive over them slowly. Do not swerve.
items.official: Rumble Strips Ahead signs warn motorists of black or orange strips placed across the travel lanes in advance of work zones, including a flagger or lane closure. Rumble strips should be slowly driven over, not swerved around.
items.mnemonic: Bumpy strips: go slow, go straight, no swerve.

items.title: Slow moving vehicle: 25 MPH
items.simple: An orange triangle on a vehicle means it travels at 25 MPH or less. Farm equipment, horse-drawn vehicles and highway work vehicles must show it. Be ready to change your speed or your position on the road.
items.official: Slow Moving Vehicles traveling at 25 MPH or less, such as farm equipment, horse-drawn vehicles or highway work vehicles, must display these signs when using a public highway. Be prepared to adjust your speed or position when you see a vehicle with one of these signs.

items.title: Pink signs: incident areas
items.simple: Pink and black signs warn you about an incident area ahead. Orange signs are for construction. Pink signs are for incidents. Slow down and use caution.
items.official: Orange and black and pink and black signs are used to advise and warn in construction (orange) and incident (pink) areas.

items.title: Black-and-white rules in work zones
items.simple: Orange or pink signs may come with black and white signs. The black and white signs give rules. Some of these rules exist only because of the road work or the incident. Obey them.
items.official: Orange and black and pink and black signs are used to advise and warn in construction (orange) and incident (pink) areas. They are used with black and white signs that convey regulations that might exist only because of the construction effort or the incident.
items.mnemonic: Orange warns. Black and white is the law.

items.title: Green signs: destinations
items.simple: Green and white signs give destination information. They help you find the places you are going.
items.official: Green and white, blue and white, and brown and white signs are used to provide helpful information. The green sign is used to provide destination types of information.
items.mnemonic: Green = Go places. Blue = services. Brown = history.

items.title: Blue signs: motorist services
items.simple: Blue and white signs tell you about services for drivers. This one shows gas and a place to sleep.
items.official: The blue sign is used to inform regarding motorists services.
items.mnemonic: Blue = services for you, like gas and a bed.

items.title: Brown signs: historic places
items.simple: Brown and white signs point out historical or cultural places in the area.
items.official: The brown sign is used to advise of historical or cultural interests that might exist in the area.
